Shuah
SHOO-ah
n. (proper, a son of Abraham by Keturah; also a Canaanite whose daughter Judah married)
Hebrew Shuwach, a pit or depression. Two men bear the name, and keeping them apart matters: one is Abraham's son by Keturah, ancestor of Bildad the Shuhite; the other is the Canaanite father-in-law of Judah.

Biblical Definition

The first Shuah is the last named of Keturah's six sons: “And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah” (Genesis 25:2). Abraham gave gifts to these sons and sent them eastward, away from Isaac, while Isaac received all that he had. From this line comes Bildad the Shuhite, one of Job's three friends. The second Shuah is a Canaanite, and the marriage is recorded as a step downward: “And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her” (Genesis 38:2). That marriage produced Er, Onan and Shelah, and Genesis 38 goes on to Tamar, the two sons who died, and the twins Pharez and Zarah. “And in process of time the daughter of Shuah Judah's wife died” (Genesis 38:12) is the verse that sets the rest of that grim chapter in motion.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a son of Abraham by Keturah, and separately as a Canaanite whose daughter Judah married.

expand to see more

KETURAH, n. The wife whom Abraham took after the death of Sarah, and the mother of six sons.

CONCUBINE, n. A woman who cohabits with a man without being his lawful wife; in Scripture, a secondary wife of inferior rank.

SHUHITE, n. A descendant of Shuah the son of Abraham; the designation of Bildad, one of Job's friends.

CANAANITE, n. A descendant of Canaan the son of Ham; one of the peoples whose daughters Israel was forbidden to marry.

LINEAGE, n. Race; progeny; descendants in a line from a common progenitor.

Key Scripture

Genesis 25:2 — "And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah."

Genesis 38:2 — "And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her."

Genesis 38:12 — "And in process of time the daughter of Shuah Judah's wife died; and Judah was comforted, and went up unto his sheepshearers to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite. in"

Genesis 25:6 — "But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country."

Modern Corruption

Marriage is now judged almost entirely by attraction and compatibility, and Genesis 38 opens with Judah seeing a Canaanite woman and taking her — a sentence written in the same grammar the chapter goes on to indict.

expand to see more

Genesis 38:2 is written to be noticed: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite... and he took her. Saw, took — the grammar of Eve at the tree and of David on the roof. The chapter that follows is one of the bleakest in the Bible: two sons so wicked that the LORD slew them, a daughter-in-law wronged, a disguise at the gate of Enaim, and Judah pronouncing a death sentence on a woman he had wronged himself. Nothing in it is presented as a model, and the root of it is in the second verse. Marriage in Scripture is a covenant made under God, not a transaction begun by sight.

The other Shuah gives the counterweight. Abraham's sons by Keturah were given gifts and sent away eastward, and one of their descendants, Bildad the Shuhite, turns up centuries later arguing theology with Job. Meanwhile the ruined chapter in Judah's life produced Pharez, and Pharez stands in the genealogy of Christ, with Tamar named in Matthew 1 among the women. God does not excuse what Judah did; he works through it and beyond it, and puts the record in the book so that no one may imagine the line to the Messiah ran through respectable people.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Shuwach (H7770), a pit; Qetuwrah (H6989), Keturah, incense; Shuchiy (H7747), Shuhite; Kenaaniy (H3669), Canaanite.

expand to see more

Hebrew Shuwach (H7770) — Shuah, a pit or depression; Abraham's son by Keturah.

Hebrew Qetuwrah (H6989) — Keturah, incense; the wife Abraham took after Sarah.

Hebrew Shuchiy (H7747) — Shuhite; Bildad's designation, from this line.

Hebrew Shuwa (H7770) — the Canaanite Shuah of Genesis 38, a different man.

Hebrew Perets (H6557) — Pharez, a breach; the son through whom the line ran to Christ.

Usage

"“Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah”."

"“Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite” — saw, and took."

"“The daughter of Shuah Judah's wife died” — and the chapter turns."
